gen-nixie-one-fs-public-sans: Hairline-thin strokes that never change width give Nixie One its faint, retro-tech glow. Public Sans sits beneath with a hefty lowercase and broad counters, a plain sans that stays friendly across paragraphs.
gen-nixie-one-general-sans: Nixie One draws its nostalgic, retro-tech heading with open curves and a constant stroke from top to baseline. General Sans fills the line generously.
gen-nixie-one-gf-orbit: Wiry, retro, and a bit dreamy. Nixie One is best at one steady stroke and open curves, while Orbit, a sans-serif, keeps each character floating apart in a rope-like line.
gen-nixie-one-work-sans: One unbroken stroke runs through every Nixie One letter. Work Sans feels brisker and more contemporary beside it, with its tight joins and open c tips adding a modern edge.
gen-orbitron-archivo: Wide-set, neon-tube lettering. Orbitron spaces its letters far apart at a single track width, which looks sharpest in a heading, while Archivo underneath is a plain sans with outward-opening curves and a commanding x-height.
gen-orbitron-manrope: Manrope brings bright open gaps at every curve and a pen line that holds one width throughout, a friendly counterpart to Orbitron. Its minimal cap-to-lowercase step is the pair's best quality.
gen-orbitron-satoshi: Precise, spaced-out, almost engineered. Orbitron lays its wide letters along the line with large open e shapes, and Satoshi follows with a soaring x-height and a sans that never looks squeezed.
gen-orbitron-work-sans: Letters spread far apart, each e with a large clear eye: that is Orbitron's whole character. And Work Sans, contemporary and modern, brings c tips that never creep toward touching.
gen-poppins-fs-erode: Erode brings a dignified text serif with a gentle ebb and flow of stroke weight. Poppins, geometric and pipe-cleaner simple, gives that softness a crisp, approachable counterpart in the heading.
gen-press-start-2p-gf-aldrich: Pixel-blocky letters pinned far apart, with a modulation you only notice up close, make Press Start 2P instantly playful. Aldrich, a modern sans-serif, answers with strips of equal width.
